newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Median annual Australian income A$15,000 - ABS.
newsitem.headline: Median annual Australian income A$15,000 - ABS.

text.p: Australia's median annual income increased less than nine percent in the five years to 1996, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Tuesday.

Releasing details of the latest census of the population, the bureau said the median annual income for people aged 15 and over increased to A$15,184, or A$292 a week, from A$13,936 -- A$268 a week in 1991.
The proportion of rich and poor changed little over the five years between each census.
About 57 percent of people over 15 earned less than A$21,000 in 1996, while only 1.8 percent were in the top income bracket of A$78,000 a year or more, the bureau said.
The 1991 census measures were slightly different, but 57 percent earned less than A$20,000 annually and about 1.9 percent were in the top bracket of A$60,000 or more.
